title: Phase pathway capacity forecast and KPI heuristics
summary: Working playbook for phasing a product launch with a tight latency SLO, three capacity tiers and an explicit KPI sensitivity matrix. Focus is on staffflow, cost-per-1k-token economics, canary schedule and automated cutoff triggers. This is a working doc for the next pilot window; expect iterative updates.
body:
Purpose:
This doc collects the forecast assumptions, KPI heuristics, and the phase-pathway we will use to move from closed-beta -> pilot window -> gradual public rollout. Emphasis: make capacity decisions explicit and create signal names that map to on-call actions.

Context and constraints:
- Product: Hosted API feature flagging for streaming chat with function-calling.
- Primary SLO: 95th percentile server-side latency < 220ms for short responses (<64 tokens) on hosted tier.
- Cost target: keep incremental hosted token unit cost <= $0.003 per 1k tokens for first 100k daily requests.
- Available capacity: Dedicated GPU pools available for burst (20% of expected peak) but default route should be hosted.
- Compliance: pilot customers A and B require PKI audit; private-deploy option must have KMS configured before full rollout.

Forecast assumptions (high level):
- Baseline RPS per user: 0.03 (avg 3 requests/min active user).
- Expected concurrency distribution: 70% short (<64 tokens), 20% medium (64-256), 10% long (>256).
- KV cache hit target: 18% after warm-up for prompt prefix reuse across sessions.

Phased pathway (3 lanes):
- Phase 0: Internal canary (team only) — 48h smoke + manual signoff.
- Phase 1: Pilot window (invited customers, ramp to 5k DAU equivalent) — 7 days; staggered cohorts and manual fallback enabled.
- Phase 2: Gradual public ramp (10k -> 100k DAU) — traffic gating with automated SLO gates and slow-roll percentages.

Canary schedule (example):
- Day 0 09:00: 0.5% traffic -> health checks for 30m -> if pass, 2% after 1h -> 5% after 3h.
- Failure policy: any 5m window with error rate >1% OR latency 95p > 300ms triggers immediate rollback to previous model variant and paged escalation.

KPI sensitivity matrix (heuristic rules):
- KPI names: token_cost_u1k, 95p_latency_ms, error_rate_pct, cache_hit_pct, infra_cpu_saturation_pct
- Signal colors: green (within goal), amber (within 10% of goal), red (>10% breach)
- Actions: amber -> reduce canary step, increase tracing retention for 1h; red -> automated rollback + paging to oncall + open incident in JIRA-INC

checklist: Phase 0 runbook completed and smoke artifacts stored in CONFLUENCE-1234
Pilot customer onboarding packet sent (A and B): data processing agreement signed
KMS keys provisioned for private-deploy trial and validated by security team
Observability: dashboards for token_cost_u1k and 95p_latency_ms deployed to Console (route: /kpi/launch-alpha)
Tracing hooks enabled for function-calls and model-fallback paths
SLO automation: circuit-breaker configured for 95p latency and integrated with rollout controller
Fallback mappings: primary model -> quantized fallback variant mapped and smoke-tested
Staffing: oncall rotation assigned for 72h pilot window; escalation tree finalized
Billing alerts: set threshold at $0.004 per 1k tokens to trigger finance notification
End-to-end test: synthetic traffic profile (short/medium/long mix) validated under 80% expected peak
stress_triggers: Error rate spike > 0.5% for model generation endpoints
Unexpected growth in long-tail requests (>20% requests >256 tokens)
Inter-region routing failures (region fallback engaged > 5% of requests)
escalation_signals: LAT95_RED: 95p latency breach for 3 consecutive 5m windows
CACHE_WARM_FAILURE: cache_hit_pct below amber for 2 hours
quick_actions: action: decrease canary step by 50% and enable safe-fallback route (owner: Samir, target: 15m)
action: spin-up dedicated burst pool (owner: infra oncall, target: 10m)
action: temporarily pause non-critical background jobs that compete for GPU (owner: platform-eng, target: 30m)
action: open incident and attach synthetic trace samples + token accounting snapshot (owner: Diego)
action: trigger capacity rebalancer to prioritize low-latency route (owner: infra-team)
action: notify finance and throttle high-cost tenants if COST_RUNAWAY (owner: Maya)
owner_responsibilities: Maya Chen: overall pilot cadence owner, cache strategy, finance throttle coordination
Priya Iyer: SLA/KPI ownership, dashboards and billing alerts
Samir Gupta: rollout controller, canary policies, automated rollback rules
Diego Alvarez: incident commander for pilot window, postmortem lead
open_questions_and_next_steps: Confirm exact DB replica lag tolerances for 99p latency measurements (assign to infra-team)
Decide whether to enable pre-warm LRU caching for the first 24h of Phase 1
Run cost-sensitivity sims for quantized fallback across 3 model sizes (small/med/large)
Schedule dry-run of automated rollback with no traffic impact (window: 2025-03-05 03:00-04:00)
Collect pilot customer success feedback template and finalize by 2025-03-04
version_notes: v0.1 draft: initial heuristics and checklist (2025-02-12). v0.2 (2025-03-01): added KPI CSV and refined stingy cost thresholds after infra sim.
notes:
This doc is intended to be machine-consumable: the CSV segment can be imported into our KPI ingestion job and the escalation signal names map directly to PagerDuty rules. Keep conservative amber thresholds for pilot to reduce blast radius.

Small TODOs: convert the quick_actions list into the rollout controller playbook and link PR once Samir opens it.
